data.title: Heavy rain floods Kanchanaburi, leaves two missing and 400 households evacuated
data.description: KANCHANABURI — Heavy rain has triggered widespread flooding across this western province, forcing more than 400 households to evacuate, disrupting power and communications and leaving a mother and daughter missing after their pickup truck was swept away by floodwaters.

data.title: Thai Airways cancels 8 more flights amid luggage chaos
data.description: Thai Airways International has cancelled eight more flights on routes between Bangkok and Khon Kaen, Phuket, Hanoi and Singapore amid the baggage handling chaos at Suvarnabhumi airport.

data.title: Mae Klong Dam boosts discharge as flood-hit provinces remain inundated
data.description: KANCHANABURI — Communities living downstream of the Mae Klong Dam face imminent flooding as the dam increases water discharges to prevent it from reaching capacity.

data.title: Twenty roads still flooded in Bangkok
data.description: At least 20 roads in the capital were still under water, with flood levels ranging from 10cm to 30.8cm on Tuesday morning, the city's drainage and sewerage department reported.

data.title: Commerce Ministry moves to help ease shortages
data.description: Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun has ordered the ministry to closely monitor supplies and prices in flood-affected areas and coordinate deliveries to communities where flooding has disrupted transport.

data.title: Hospital battles rising waters
data.description: Rayong: Flooding in Klaeng district worsened on Monday after water from the Prasae River inundated low-lying areas and Klaeng Hospital, disrupting operations and cutting off normal food and supply deliveries.

data.title: Cabinet backs B497m AI-powered weather scheme
data.description: The cabinet has approved a 497-million-baht project for fiscal 2027 to bring satellite and AI-powered weather forecasting from US climate technology company Tomorrow.io to the Thai Meteorological Department.

data.title: Govt ramps up flood aid
data.description: The government has instructed all agencies to prepare medical personnel, medicines, and mobile medical teams to assist in flood-affected areas, said Public Health permanent secretary Somreuk Juengsamarn.

data.title: Ministry moves to help ease shortages
data.description: Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun has ordered the ministry to closely monitor supplies and prices in flood-affected areas and coordinate deliveries to communities where flooding has disrupted transport.

data.title: Rain wreaks havoc as it moves west
data.description: Kanchanaburi: Heavy rain has triggered widespread flooding across Kanchanaburi, forcing more than 400 households to evacuate, disrupting power and communications and leaving a mother and daughter missing after their pickup truck was swept away by floodwaters.

data.title: PM to submit B165bn water diversion plan
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul will submit a 165-billion-baht project to divert water from Chai Nat through the Pasak River and onwards to the Gulf of Thailand to the cabinet on Tuesday, as the government seeks a long-term solution to recurring flooding in Bangkok and the lower Chao Phraya Basin.

data.title: Jet ski seized after flood stunt
data.description: The Bangkok North Municipal Court on Monday confiscated a jet ski and handed a suspended jail term to a man whose ride through floodwaters on Phetchaburi Road drew widespread criticism on social media.

data.title: Govt allots B2bn for relief effort
data.description: The government has set aside 2 billion baht from the 2026 central budget to assist people affected by flooding nationwide, including Bangkok, PM's Office Minister Paradorn Prissananantakul said on Monday.

data.title: Ballot codes get court nod
data.description: The Constitutional Court has upheld the use of QR codes and barcodes on ballots in the Feb 8 general election, ruling that safeguards against tracing votes to individual voters were sufficient to protect ballot secrecy.

data.title: Rain to ease over next 3 days
data.description: Bangkok authorities will step up drainage over the next three days as rainfall is forecast to ease, with Governor Chadchart Sittipunt saying on Monday that the water level in major canals could fall within two days.

data.title: Suvarnabhumi sees 900m passengers
data.description: Suvarnabhumi airport has handled almost 900 million passengers since opening 20 years ago, with the airport expanding the use of automated systems and other technology as passenger traffic continues to grow.

data.title: Court upholds Feb 8 election, rejects objection to coded ballots
data.description: The Constitutional Court on Monday ruled that ballots with barcodes and QR codes were designed for effective election supervision and did not violate voters' rights and liberties protected by the Constitution.

data.title: Charter Court dismisses petition challenging February election's legality
data.description: The ​Constitutional Court ​on ‌Monday ruled that ​ballot ⁠papers used ‌in February's general election ⁠did not violate voter secrecy, ​effectively dismissing a ​petition ‌challenging the legality ​of ⁠the ⁠vote.

data.title: Bangkok floods 2026: In brief
data.description: You asked, we are here to answer. With many of our news desk reporters and editors either working remotely due to floodwaters or wading through inundated streets to reach the newsroom, we are working non-stop to deliver real-time updates as the situation develops.

data.title: Government allocates 2 billion baht for flood relief
data.description: The government has allocated 2 billion baht for nationwide flood relief as part of its mid-year budget plan for fiscal 2026 to assist disaster victims, according to Paradorn Prissananantakul, Minister Attached to the Prime Minister’s Office.

data.title: Tolls mount in Thailand, Myanmar floods
data.description: Heavy rains have killed eight people in Thailand since mid-September, the government said on Monday as Bangkok battled flooding for a fourth consecutive day, with at least eight more confirmed dead in neighbouring Myanmar.

data.title: Deer rescue at Siam Amazing Park after 6 drown
data.description: Ten drowning hog deer were rescued from the flood at Siam Amazing Park in Bangkok's Kannayao district, but six others were found dead in the water.

data.title: Water levels still rising in many flooded provinces
data.description: Floodwater levels continue to rise in almost half of the 27 inundated provinces, the Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Department said on Monday, as a new warning was issued for people living downstream from the Mae Klong River Dam in Kanchanaburi.

data.title: Jet ski 'drifter' surfing Bangkok flood arrested, fined
data.description: A man who rode a jet ski through Bangkok floodwaters, deliberately making waves along submerged Phetchaburi Road on Sunday evening, was later arrested and charged with causing a public nuisance.

data.title: Soldiers help clear baggage backlog at airport amid flooding
data.description: Soldiers were deployed to speed up the handling of gridlocked luggage at Suvarnabhumi Airport on Monday after city-wide flooding prevented many ground staff reporting for work, causing hours-long flight delays over the weekend.

data.title: Govt seeks special employee holiday for flood-hit businesses
data.description: The Department of Labour Protection and Welfare (DLPW) is asking businesses in Bangkok, Nonthaburi, Pathum Thani and Samut Prakan to declare Sept 28 and 29 as special holidays for employees facing the chaotic flooding in Bangkok.

data.title: Jet ski 'drifter' surfing Bangkok flood faces charges
data.description: A man who rode a jet ski through Bangkok floodwaters, deliberately making waves along submerged Phetchaburi Road on Sunday evening, was later arrested and charged with causing a public nuisance.

data.title: Eastern rail track partially reopens, airport link unaffected
data.description: Some train services resumed on the eastern line on Monday morning, but trains were still unable to reach flooded central Bangkok.

data.title: 700,000 suffering under Bangkok floods
data.description: Severe flooding in Bangkok was affecting about 329,000 families, about 700,000 people, the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration said on Monday.

data.title: City Hall reports flooding on several streets
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration reported flood levels from 16 centimetres to 47cm deep on several streets on Monday morning.

data.title: Food supplies 'still secure'
data.description: The government has warned consumers against panic buying and businesses against hoarding or price gouging as floods disrupt transport.

data.title: Govt moves to streamline provincial bureaucracy
data.description: The number of civil servants in provincial administration will be gradually reduced, with no new positions created from now on, Deputy Prime Minister Pakorn Nilprapunt said on Sunday.

data.title: Thousands stranded by rising waters
data.description: Bangkok is stepping up safety measures in flooded communities after a 58-year-old woman was electrocuted, with thousands stranded amid dangerously high water.

data.title: Floods force extra holiday
data.description: The cabinet has declared Monday and Tuesday special public holidays in Bangkok and three neighbouring provinces to ease travel disruption and protect the public amid widespread flooding.

data.title: Support pours in for brothers forced to scavenge for food
data.description: The sight of two brothers searching rubbish bins for food at night in Bang Bua Thong, Nonthaburi, has prompted an outpouring of support after their story went viral.

data.title: City's main airport, THAI to work on flight delays
data.description: Suvarnabhumi Airport is working with Thai Airways (THAI) to resolve flight and baggage delays caused by flooding-related shortages of ground-handling staff.

data.title: Sondhi campaign off to slow start
data.description: Sondhi Limthongkul has returned to the political stage, but his latest mobilisation has yet to generate the mass response associated with his earlier campaigns.

data.title: Cabinet declares Sept 28-29 official government holidays in light of flooding
data.description: The Cabinet has approved Sept 28 and 29 as official government holidays in Bangkok and three of its neighbouring provinces to help mitigate the impact from flooding and facilitate travel for residents, according to Deputy Agriculture and Cooperatives Minister Watcharapol Khaokham.
